source: synthetic weather fixture, not live data
note: SYNTHETIC COMPETITION DEMO FIXTURE -- not Open-Meteo historical data and not a real forecast. Hand-authored TrailGuard replay asset for Phase 5 benchmark scenario B06 (future gust front) and B11 (multi-driver storm). The scenario's projected arrival instants fall between 12:10 and 14:40, so this file only covers the window a hiker on this clock actually reaches, and the gust ramp meets them there: 28 km/h at 12:00, 50 km/h at 13:00, 72 km/h at 14:00, 74 km/h at 15:00. The R-C gust threshold in the frozen rule pack is 45 km/h, so a scenario whose analysis clock sits at 12:10 reads a safe NOW row and a hazardous +30 row from the SAME file -- which is the point: only the horizon changes. Values are invented. precipitation_probability arrives in percent ('%' in hourly_units, exactly as open-meteo reports it) and must be divided by 100 to obtain the 0..1 probability the TrailGuard schemas use.
